body:
Duke's Dame Sarr and Alabama's Brandon Garrison were also among the players who stood out. Here is what you need to know from Thursday's exhibition games
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:29 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026-27 college basketball season begins in just over three weeks, meaning the top programs around the country will be playing in various open (and closed-door) scrimmages throughout the next month in preparation for the season. A handful of teams played their first scrimmage of the season on Thursday, including Duke, Alabama and LSU.Duke faced Belmont on Thursday night at Cameron Indoor Stadium, which gave college basketball fans a glimpse of a roster expected to open the season ranked No. 2 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll. Furthermore, it was the first look at several newcomers on the roster, including Wisconsin transfer John Blackwell and incoming five-star freshman big man Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje.Boumtje Boumtje stole the show and showed why he should be the favorite to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2028 NBA Draft. He finished with a team-high 19 points in 22 minutes and shot 7 of 11 from the field during the Blue Devils' 102-62 win over Belmont. Duke was without veteran guard Caleb Foster — the projected starter at point guard — for its first exhibition game due to an ankle injury.
        
            
                SEC expert picks: 2026-27 preview, projected order of finish, preseason predictions, top players to watch
                
                    David Cobb                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
LSU's roster construction under Will Wade, who is returning for his second stint as the Tigers' coach, has been under a microscope this offseason. For the past several weeks, LSU has listed just four players on the team's website due to almost half of the roster being in eligibility limbo because of holding out for a fifth year, or international players who hadn't been cleared to play.
The Tigers played just seven players in the 63-60 win over McNeese, which included former UCLA star Donovan Dent making his debut with his new team.With the first wave of scrimmages in the books, here are the biggest takeaways from Thursday.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Will JBB be Duke's best player in 2027?After watching Boumtje Boumtje make his debut in a college uniform, it's very obvious why he should be the consensus favorite to go No. 1 in 2028. Boumtje Boumtje, who doesn't turn 18 until May 30 and will play the entire 2026-27 season at 17 years old, is not eligible for next summer's draft due to the NBA's age requirement, which requires players to be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. Boumtje Boumtje isn't the only newcomer in college basketball who falls under that umbrella, as Texas' Marcus Spears Jr. and UCLA's Nikola Kusturica will each have to play at least two seasons of college basketball before declaring for the draft.
One of the top position battles coming into the season was who Duke would start at power forward next to veteran big man Patrick Ngongba II, with Boumtje Boumtje and fellow five-star Cameron Williams serving as the top contenders to occupy that spot. Duke coach Jon Scheyer started Boumtje Boumtje in its first scrimmage, which is a strong indication that he has the inside track to hold onto that starting spot.
Boumtje Boumtje had a complete game against Belmont that showcased a little bit of everything in his game. Above all else, what stood out about his performance is how clean his shot mechanics look for a 7-foot-2 big man who is just 17 years old. He attempted five 3-pointers against Belmont and knocked down two of them. He also finished with two blocks, two steals and seven rebounds in just 22 minutes of action.Duke has arguably the deepest roster in college basketball. Still, it wouldn't be surprising to see Boumtje Boumtje, who was named preseason ACC Freshman of the Year by CBS Sports, emerge as Duke's best player at some point this season. He is far too talented not to play him at least 25-30 minutes per game, and maybe even more.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brandon Garrison looks like a great fit at AlabamaAlabama opened the scrimmage cycle with a 111-93 win over Furman behind a team-high 19 points from Amari Allen. Despite being without Aden Holloway — who is serving a suspension following an incident earlier this spring — the Crimson Tide posted 111 points and showcased why the program will be one of the highest-scoring offenses in the country under Nate Oats.One player who stood out in particular was Brandon Garrison, who came off the bench and finished with 15 points, four rebounds and a block. Garrison, who played at Kentucky the last two seasons, didn't miss a shot (7-for-7) and looked like a perfect fit in Alabama's system.
After the game, Oats gave Garrison high praise and said that Garrison may be the "best passing big man" he's coached.
"He can really handle the ball," Oats said. "He may be the best passing big I've ever coached. He can really pass. We will try and use that a little bit more."
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU still has hurdles to clear before its season-openerLSU went with a seven-man rotation during its first scrimmage of the year against McNeese. The Tigers received good news before the game when Michael Ružić, one of five international players Wade recruited this offseason, was ruled eligible for the 2026-27 season. He finished with 11 points and 16 rebounds in 34 minutes.Ružić started next to Divine Ugochukwu, Donovan Dent, Abdi Bashir Jr. and Mouhamed Dioubate. Notable players who didn't play who Wade recruited this offseason: Skyy Clark, RJ Luis Jr., Saliou Niang, Brice Dessert and Gilad Levy.
LSU still has hurdles to clear before the season opens up next month. Clark, Dent, and Luis are part of five-for-five lawsuits, while Niang, Dessert, and Levy are international players who hope to get cleared in time before the start of the season. Wade has said himself that his roster building has been "unconventional." If all those players are ruled eligible, LSU will be in a position to compete in the top half of the SEC. However, time is running out for that to happen.
        
            
                Tracking Will Wade's 'unconventional' roster at LSU: Who's eligible and who's on the outside looking in?
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Is Dame Sarr ready for a Year 2 breakout?While Boumtje Boumtje was the player from Duke's roster who stood out the most, Sarr also had a very strong showing. The former five-star forward started 30 of 38 games for Duke last season and looked primed for a larger role this year.Sarr looked noticeably stronger and more aggressive in hunting his shot. Sarr was used mostly as a catch-and-shoot 3-point specialist during his freshman season at Duke, with 133 of his 208 total field goal attempts last season coming from beyond the arc.
Although it's a very small sample size — and a scrimmage at that — what really stood out is how much contact Sarr drew. He got to the free-throw line a team-high 10 times and finished with 19 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Sarr attempted 62 free throws total and only connected on 53.2% of those attempts. Improved free-throw volume and knocking them down at a higher clip will do wonders for his game. Sarr looks like a potential riser as a 3-and-D 6-foot-8 wing that could put himself in the conversation to be a first-round pick in 2027.In my way-too-early 2027 mock draft, I had Sarr going No. 26 overall. He could find himself getting picked somewhere in the teens if this rise and improvement continue, especially because the 2027 class as a whole lacks true consensus. Sarr isn't going to post eye-popping stats this season because of how deep Duke's roster is, but his archetype is coveted at the NBA level.

title: Big Ten Media Days takeaways: Inside Oregon's scramble, Michigan's encore and The David Mirkovic Show begins - CBS Sports
description: CHICAGO -- Dana Altman first confided in long-time assistant Tony Stubblefield that he was considering retirement last Friday. Stubblefi
body:
CHICAGO -- Dana Altman first confided in long-time assistant Tony Stubblefield that he was considering retirement last Friday. Stubblefield waited for the weekend to pass, hoping his friend would have a change of heart. Altman wanted to meet with Oregon athletic director Rob Mullens on Monday, but Mullens was out of town, so the summit was kicked down the road for 24 more hours. Late Tuesday, Altman relayed to Stubblefield that he was still leaning toward hanging it up, but he wanted to sleep on it one more night.After Wednesday's practice, Oregon's players gathered for a meeting. Senior wing Andrew Meadow thought they might be getting fresh new shoes. Instead, Altman dropped the bombshell that he was stepping away, despite being on the doorstep of the exclusive 800 Wins Club. "We had a challenging year last year," Stubblefield said. "Not that it had anything bearing on coach's decision, but I think that took a lot out of him."Stubblefield was elevated to the interim head coach, which meant he had to pack a jet-black suit and hop on a late-Wednesday flight bound for Chicago ahead of Thursday's Big Ten Media Days. 
The biggest brouhaha now is the portal. Since Oregon's brass tabbed Stubblefield as the interim coach, Oregon's roster cannot enter the portal until Nov. 7, five days after the Ducks' season-opener against Montana. Exiting Eugene now would mean giving up a season of games and NIL payments to try and transfer over Christmas break? That's a lot of hoops to jump through."We've had positive feedback from the majority of the guys that we've been to get ahold of their families and their representation," Stubblefield said. "I will get back to Oregon immediately after this today, and schedule some one-on-one meetings with our players and go over things with them and continue to work the phone and be traveling, I'm sure, over the course of the next three or four days. We feel like we have a really good group of young men, resilient young men in that locker room, a very talented group of players that we want to keep this group intact, because we felt like we did a great job attacking the portal and bringing in a high school kid or two. We have 11 new guys, and we feel like we have a chance to really make a step in the right direction and get back to the NCAA tournament."David Mirkovic helped lead Illinois on a Final Four run last season 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            The David Mirkovic Show beginsThe Big Ten's preseason groupthink can agree on two fronts:1. Michigan State's Jeremy Fears Jr. is the consensus Preseason Player of the Year.
2. Illinois' David Mirkovic is going to be a total stud this year.Illinois isn't running from it. A broken foot was the lone hiccup amid an outstanding summer that has the Illini coaching staff believing Mirkovic is destined to be Illinois' next first-round pick."Dynamic young man, just a dynamic player, one of the best players in the country with just an incredible personality," Illinois coach Brad Underwood said. "Mirk loves life. I think he's great for the sport. He's always happy. He never has a bad day. Great charisma, sense of humor. When you get to know him, you'll find out how intelligent he is. He's just got a quick wit to him.  And then you step across the line, and he's that guy that just, you know, wants to rip your throat out and compete. I'm excited for the world to get to know him."Mirkovic's hilarious quotes and goofy antics perhaps shadowed just how dominant his freshman season was. Mirkovic averaged 13.6 points, 7.9 rebounds and 2.7 assists while shooting 38% from downtown on more than 4.0 attempts per game. Rival coaches like Minnesota's Niko Medved, Purdue's Matt Painter and Nebraska's Fred Hoiberg gushed over Mirkovic's skill-set repeatedly. The 6-9 forward also notched a historic 29-point, 17-rebound performance in the Illini's NCAA Tournament romp over Penn. Mirkovic became just the third freshman in NCAA Tournament history with 25+ points and 15+ rebounds in an NCAA Tournament game, per CBB Analytics.

        
            
                Big Ten expert picks: Projected order of finish, preseason predictions, top players to watch, starting lineups
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
By the end of the season, Mirkovic had turned into Illinois' second-best player, behind eventual lottery-pick Keaton Wagler. Now, he is slated to be the go-to piece of a top-five Illinois squad that was picked to win the Big Ten. "I loved his skill set," Underwood said when asked for his first impression of Mirkovic when he was playing for SC Derby in the Balkans. "He was a guy that didn't shoot a lot of threes, but I love his ability to make threes. He was a tenacious rebounder. I was obviously drawn to that. "He was a fat. I called him fat. He was just a fat guy that played in the post, but he had a tenacity and a toughness to him. He's better than I thought in terms of being able to handle the ball. But we needed him as a good counter to Tomi (Ivisic) at the time with physicality, and now he's turned into a pretty skilled basketball player."
Inside Michigan's new offensive coordinatorThe reigning champions will have a new offensive coordinator after Dusty May left for the Dallas Mavericks and two Michigan assistants — specifically Drew Williamson and ex-New Zealand Breakers head coach Mody Maor — followed May to the league. New Michigan coach Mike Boynton hired Brown coach Mike Martin in July to run the offense alongside ex-Orlando Magic staffer Dylan Murphy.It was a bit of a curious hire because Brown's offense ranked 342nd nationally last season, including ranking dead last in Ivy League play in efficiency. But style of play may be at the epicenter of this new marriage. Michigan bulldozed its way to the title, partly by running one of the nation's most efficient cutting offenses. Michigan had stud creators like Elliot Cadeau, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Aday Mara to generate advantages, and it used cutting (and a lot of unselfishness) to convert those advantages into buckets.   Martin's offenses have annually rated well above average in … the number of shots that came directly off a cut. 
2025-26: 79th percentile in frequency2024-25: 65th percentile 2023-24: 67th percentile2022-23: 78th percentile2021-22: 76th percentile2020-21: No season due to COVID2019-20: 93rd percentile2018-19: 62nd percentile2017-18: 76th percentile "Mike and I have talked hoops a lot," Boynton said. "I think it's a little deeper than just watching a guy's team playing or how they score. It's more like being able to understand what they're doing and how they're trying to operate, relative to how you want to play. If I was going to play a system where you throw the ball inside 50 times a game, like if I had Shaq? Maybe Mike is not the best coach. He's not coached a style like that. But the way we play is the way he coached before. The combination of him and Dylan Murphy together, two really, really smart basketball people, it's going to give us a chance to be efficient on that end of the floor."Boynton has reiterated often that he doesn't want to reinvent the wheel offensively in the post-May era. That trickles down to lineup construction as well. Michigan is hoping to get Roddy Gayle Jr. eligible for a fifth year, and he'll start at the 3-spot next to Cadeau and Trey McKenney if he gets good news from the judicial system later this month. If not? Michigan is exploring another jumbo lineup with prized 6-10 freshman Quinn Costello operating at the 3 next to Michigan's new-look front-line of 6-11 forward JP Estrella and 7-2 center Moustapha Thiam. It mostly works because Costello is a lights-out shooter and prefers to float around the perimeter at this point. "That lineup is very good," Cadeau said. "Like, we'll be able to stretch the floor a lot. I feel like me and Mo or JP in a ball screen. Trey and Quinn in the corners, like nobody can help off Trey or Quinn, so it'll kind of give me the freedom and the wide-open space that I need."

        
            
                Big Ten basketball preseason poll, predictions 2026-27: Michigan, Purdue overrated; USC, Iowa underrated
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Quick hits1. The Antione West Jr. hype has left the station at Purdue The 6-3 combo guard redshirted last season, but Purdue coach Matt Painter believes he is poised for a massive breakout season ... even if he's still coming off the bench to start the 2026-27 campaign."Antione West is a really good two-way player. He's a plus-five, plus-six wingspan, very, very good on the basketball, good at creating for himself, good combo guard," Painter said. "We just had a deep backcourt [last year]. How much was he going to play? Who was it going to affect? I compared it to Patrick Mahomes not playing instead of Alex Smith, who was a great quarterback in the NFL, and then learning that year. Then, all of a sudden, Patrick Mahomes, in a quick amount of time, was the best player in the NFL. He's going to be one of the better guards in our league." 2. Michigan State has another massive breakout candidate in shooting guard Jordan Scott
Scott worked his way into the rotation using defense last year and is poised to be a Day One starter for a deep Spartans' club that has Detroit in its sights this season."Jordan's made huge improvement," Fears said. "He got way more athletic. He's been dunking more and he's finally like growing into his body. I think he's kind of a late bloomer. But overall, he makes shots, he defends, he's tough, gets every loose ball. He's just a winning player."3. Mick Cronin had a Mick Cronin moment again, this time at my expense.Everybody's got an opinion on the UCLA coach. He's not perfect, but I like him, and his sense of humor is usually right up my alley. So Cronin messing with me a little bit about how much prized Texas Tech transfer Jaylen Petty will play on the ball this season is totally fine.
Anyways, here's the clip.

title: Misunderstood Shedeur Sanders opens up on public perception as Browns QB: 'Why would people think this?' - CBS Sports
description: What the second-year quarterback told Cosmopolitan this week about how he's viewed nationally
body:
What the second-year quarterback told Cosmopolitan this week about how he's viewed nationally
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:47 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Shedeur Sanders hasn't been in the spotlight this season due to the Browns' 3-1 start with Deshaun Watson as Cleveland's starter, and it sounds like he's fine with taking a backseat to media scrutiny for the first time in his career.In a wide-ranging interview this week with Cosmopolitan that was conducted earlier this summer, Sanders said he's still coming to grips with being routinely misjudged by the public."I wish people understood me more as a human being," Sanders said. "I don't think a lot of people really know me. I'm just now starting to understand that. You hear a lot of things online, but every encounter I have in person, people end up saying, 'Oh, wow, he's actually a great guy.' Why would you think I'm a bad guy? "So I've been looking at things a lot more lately, like, 'Why would people think this?' It's not something I'm going to put (solely) on myself, but I do want to fix that. I want to connect with more people, so they can meet me and see the truth."
Sanders told the magazine he "lives" in his own world and can't remember the last time he has looked at social media banter surrounding his play, Cleveland's quarterback situation or anything relating to football.The pre-draft experience for Sanders and his rollercoaster first 1.5 seasons in the NFL is well-documented. His brother streamed much of his NFL Draft party in April 2025, which included the raw emotion and initial shock of being skipped over for Louisville's Tyler Shough at No. 40 overall in the second round, along with a prank call impersonating New Orleans Saints general manager Mickey Loomis. Later came the reports of Sanders sandbagging certain interviews, deciding not to throw at the combine and how he handled the process, all directly affecting his draft slide.
Sanders has tried to explain the misinterpretations surrounding him before. Prior to his rookie season last fall in the NFL, Sanders attributed "99% of hatred" directed at him toward his father, Colorado coach and Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders."I'm just his son, but (the kids) didn't grow up in an era to where they watched him play," Shedeur Sanders said during a 2025 interview with Cleveland.com after he was picked in the fifth round. "It's just the older generation that does it to me rather than the younger people. Because when I come in person, there's no negativity I see. But it's all over online."Sanders' future with the BrownsWhile the Browns would reportedly "welcome a deal" for the right price involving Sanders or Dillon Gabriel since they have four quarterbacks on the roster, nothing appears imminent ahead of next month's NFL trade deadline.
Browns insider Mary Kay Cabot said Thursday, "anything can happen over the next three weeks" before stressing the franchise would be okay with keeping its deep quarterback room as is.Sanders battled with Watson throughout camp and the preseason before first-year coach Todd Monken ultimately went with the former first-rounder.Sanders has made appearances in two games this season, including one pass thrown against the Carolina Panthers in Week 3. In eight games last fall as a first-year player, Sanders completed 120-of-212 pass attempts for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
Monken said Wednesday he was "looking forward" to seeing Gabriel back on the field following his return from injured reserve. He's expected to push Sanders for the No. 2 spot behind Watson moving forward.The Browns, who are in a first-place tie in the AFC North with Baltimore, play the Jets in New York on Sunday, hoping to move out front.
